top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a new pharmacological principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase with catalytic removal of the target, reaching proteins without conventional pockets and reproduced independently for two decades. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept and Handa the cereblon mechanism of approved thalidomide-type drugs, which answers the clinical-maturity objection and ties the strands into one story. I rank the Ciulli trio (P003) second because I accept that the PROTAC and glue lineages may be judged separate, and then structure-guided design is the better single-strand credit. C-N coupling (P001) has clean credit and maturity but sits close to the 2010 prize; the lipid nanoparticle prize (P005) is clinically proven but its three-name credit is contested; Car-Parrinello (P004) is sound but less close to my field; no award is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; modest scientific overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly of peptide-lipid systems, relevant to P005, but no personal or institutional tie to any proposed laureate
